skill.name: role-creator
skill.description: Create and maintain Codex custom-agent TOML files with validation, templates, and install helpers.
skill.summary: Build Codex custom agents as standalone TOML role files.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples or expected local Codex configuration writes. The installer intentionally edits hidden Codex config files, and the full template can pass an API-key environment variable to an MCP server. One additional medium-risk issue was found where MCP server names are interpolated into a generated TOML expression without escaping.

remediation.issue: Persistent writes to ~/.codex/config.toml and ~/.codex/agents are part of the install workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Keep explicit confirmation before writes, default to project-scoped paths when possible, and document the backup and rollback path clearly.

remediation.issue: The full template enables an MCP server with LINEAR_API_KEY in env_vars.
remediation.suggestion: Mark the template as advanced, keep it opt-in, and warn users that named environment variables may be shared with the configured MCP server.

remediation.issue: MCP server names are inserted into a generated expression without escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Validate MCP server names against a strict identifier pattern or pass names as jq variables instead of interpolating them into expr.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe MCP server name interpolation
semantic_findings.description: scripts/write_role_config.sh trims MCP server names from --mcp-enable and --mcp-disable, then inserts each name into a generated jq/tomlq expression. A name containing quotes or expression syntax could corrupt the generated configuration command.

content.value_statement: Creating Codex roles by hand is error-prone because each agent needs valid TOML, required fields, and the right scope. This skill guides users through inputs, writes role files, and validates the result.
actual_capabilities: Collects required role details before writing a custom-agent TOML file.
Creates minimal or advanced Codex role configurations from command-line options.
Supports global and project-scoped agent file locations.
Adds optional nickname, sandbox, web search, and MCP settings when requested.
Validates generated TOML against expected required keys and allowed configuration fields.
limitations: Requires local shell utilities such as tomlq and jq for helper scripts.
Does not verify that a generated agent performs well on real tasks.
Advanced MCP and network settings need careful user review before use.
Examples target Codex custom-agent configuration, not general Claude agent setup.

use_cases.title: Create a focused review agent
use_cases.description: Generate a role file for code review with clear instructions, model choice, and reasoning effort.

use_cases.title: Standardize team agent templates
use_cases.description: Build reusable role templates that keep custom agents consistent across projects.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot role registration
use_cases.description: Check role paths, required fields, and TOML validity when Codex cannot find an agent.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic role
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project-scoped Codex agent named reviewer. Ask me for any missing required values before writing the TOML file.

prompt_templates.title: Add clear instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write developer instructions for a Codex research agent. Keep the role narrow and include validation expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Generate an advanced role
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a global Codex agent with nickname candidates, read-only sandboxing, and disabled web search. Confirm every optional setting first.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and troubleshoot
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Codex role file for missing required keys, unsupported settings, and likely causes of unknown agent_type errors.

output_examples.input: Create a reviewer role for project use.
output_examples.output: A project-scoped role file is created with the requested name, description, model, reasoning effort, and developer instructions.

output_examples.input: Add nickname candidates and read-only sandboxing.
output: The role includes the confirmed nickname list.
The sandbox mode is set to read-only.
Unrequested MCP and web search settings are omitted.

output_examples.output: The validation report identifies missing required fields, unsupported keys, or confirms that the role is ready to run.

best_practices: Confirm the role name, scope, model, reasoning effort, and instructions before writing files.
Use minimal role files by default and add optional settings only when needed.
Validate TOML syntax and required keys before trying to spawn the agent.
anti_patterns: Do not copy the full advanced template without reviewing every enabled capability.
Do not store secret values in role files; reference environment variable names only when required.
Do not give broad sandbox, network, or MCP access to roles that do not need it.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates standalone TOML files that define Codex custom agents.

faq.question: Can it create project-scoped agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports project-scoped files under a project .codex agents directory.

faq.question: Can it create global agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can target the global Codex agents directory when the user confirms that scope.

faq.question: Does it require optional sandbox or MCP settings?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends minimal files unless the user explicitly requests optional settings.

faq.question: Does it validate generated files?
faq.answer: Yes. The included validation script checks TOML structure, required keys, and unsupported settings.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with secrets?
faq.answer: Do not place secret values in generated files. Review any env_vars entries before enabling MCP servers.
